# Lantern scores the referred and declined book against the underwriter of record, not against an outcome

## Context Scope

The Lantern pilot design and every number quoted in the proposal that rests on it. Roughly nine thousand referred and declined cases over eighteen months.

## Fact Statement

A declined case has no outcome, because nothing was underwritten and nothing subsequently happened that Calderwood can observe. There is therefore nothing to measure accuracy against. What the pilot can measure is agreement: how often the model reaches the same call as the underwriter who handled the case. Ruaridh Cale confirmed there is no other source, and the proposal has to use the word agreement rather than accuracy wherever it reports a number.

## Provenance

Ruaridh Cale, closing an open question first raised at the 2026-03-24 scoping call and settled at the 2026-04-28 field walkthrough. The accepted book was ruled out at scoping on the same reasoning in reverse: nothing bad happening is not a signal.

## Why This Matters

Every headline number in the proposal is a comparison against human judgement, and calling it accuracy would be a claim Calderwood can neither verify nor be held to. It also sets what the pilot can be declared successful against, which is the thing a pursuit gets wrong when the proposal and the design were written a month apart.
